newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India coconut oil imports unlikely, official says.
newsitem.headline: India coconut oil imports unlikely, official says.

text.p: India will not be importing coconut oil in the next few years because of the efforts of a very strong farmers' lobby in keeping such imports out, a senior industry official said on Friday.
H.V. Mariwala, chairman of Marson Holdings and a long-time coconut trader, said high domestic prices in India of coconut oil "should be an open invitation" for imports.
"Every time there is talk of importing coconut oil into India, the small farmers lobby is up in arms preventing a step from being taken," he said.

India's coconut production is concentrated in the southern states of Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. Some five million farm families are dependent on the coconut crop. Coconut oil is used in the country mainly for hair oil, soaps and the manufacture of fatty acids and fatty alcohols.
Mariwala said he does not see any chance for India to trade in coconut oil or other coconut products with the Philippines or Indonesia, the world's leading producer of coconut products.
"We have always been an insular country in the matter of copra and coconut oil and shall continue to be so as far as I can see," he said.
